425138.name: Rabbinical College of America
425138.note: Its own history: 'The college's first location was single family home located in Newark, New Jersey' when it was founded in 1956; 'The school moved from the Newark site in 1971' to the Morris County campus (82 acres; Wikipedia: Morris Township).

earlier.where: a single-family home in Newark

118533.name: Chabad of Paramus
118533.note: CrownHeights.info and Anash (on new shluchim joining them): 'In 2002, Shluchim Rabbi Moshe and Zeesy Grossbaum made Paramus their home'; they direct Chabad of Paramus.

117654.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Western Monmouth County
117654.note: News Transcripts (CrownHeights.info, 23 May 2006): 'Celebration 20 will offer an opportunity to reflect on the accomplishments of Chabad of Western Monmouth County' over 20 years (so 1986); its own site (2026): 'creating meaningful Jewish experiences ... for forty years'. Founded by Rabbi Boruch and Tova Chazanow; its Gan Israel day camp from 1990. (A March 2012 piece spoke of its 25th year.)

698690.name: Chabad Ventnor Shul
698690.note: The Jewish Exponent (CrownHeights.info, 19 July 2006): 'Chabad-Lubavitch has opened a storefront synagogue in the heart of Ventnor, just blocks from the beach and boardwalk. The synagogue, called Chabad at the Shore, is being run by Chabad of Atlantic County'; Rabbi Shmuel Rapoport enlisted his son Rabbi Avrohom Rapoport to run it. In June 2008 a new Ventnor location (South Jersey Jewish Times).

117655.name: Chabad at the Shore
117655.note: This listing is Chabad of Atlantic County (ChabadAC.com, Rabbi Shmuel Rapoport), today at 6605 Atlantic Avenue, Ventnor (a former church, opened Aug 2015). NJ.com (CrownHeights.info, 13 Sept 2016): 'Rabbi Rapoport's parents, Rabbi Shmuel and Tova Rapoport, were sent in 1984 by the Lubavitcher Rebbe ... to establish a Chabad-Lubavitch center for the community' (in Atlantic City). Agreeing: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 31 July 2011): 'Shmuel and Tova Rapoport first moved to the Shore close to three decades ago'; the Jewish Exponent (CrownHeights.info, 31 July 2008): 'For more than two decades, Chabad of Atlantic County has run Jewish programs throughout the South Jersey area', headquartered in Margate. Only the Jewish Exponent of 19 July 2006 differs ('a roughly 14-year-old organization based in Margate', about 1992).

earlier.where: Margate, N.J. (its headquarters, the Pinchus Kiedjan Chabad House)

117658.name: Chabad of Mercer County - Princeton
117658.note: Town Topics (3 April 2019), on its new center on Route 206: 'Princeton Chabad, founded by Dubov in 1991, previously served the Jewish community from the rabbi's residences.' Rabbi Dovid Dubov; also Chabad of Princeton and Greater Mercer County.

earlier.where: Rabbi Dovid Dubov's residences

117659.name: Chabad Center of Northwest New Jersey
117659.note: Its own site: 'established in the beginning of 1988 by a small group of volunteers'; Jewish Link: its 37th anniversary gala (June 2025) and 38th (July 2026), both counting from 1988. Rabbi Asher and Sarah Herson; it began with a few families at a local VFW hall; now One Torah Way, Rockaway.

earlier.where: a local VFW hall

117913.name: Chabad of Greater Somerset County
117913.note: Daily Record (CrownHeights.info, 25 June 2012, 'Basking Ridge Chabad Celebrates 20 Years'): 'Herson and his wife Malkie established the Chabad center in 1992'; 'established by the Hersons in a small apartment in Basking Ridge'; 'By 2004, Chabad built a new structure on its existing location at 3048 Valley Road'. Patch (its 21st anniversary): 'what began in a small Basking Ridge apartment in 1992'.

earlier.where: a small apartment in Basking Ridge

117661.name: Chabad House of Vineland
117661.note: Chabad.org obituary (CrownHeights.info, 14 Feb 2021): Rabbi Yisroel Rapoport served at the Chabad yeshivah in Los Angeles 1985 to 1987, then became rabbi of Congregation Sons of Jacob in Vineland, 'where he stayed for over 30 years', co-directing Chabad-Lubavitch of Cumberland County with his wife Nechama. So he began after 1987 and by early 1991. Exact year not found yet.

117660.name: Friends of Lubavitch of Bergen County
117660.note: A Times of Israel blog ('40 Years'): the author's 'very first day serving as a Shaliach of the Lubavitcher Rebbe with Friends of Lubavitch of Bergen county was July 1, 1982', so it existed by then; it later bought a Masonic Temple, Bergen County's first Chabad House. Rabbi Ephraim Simon. Start year not found yet.

117975.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Camden County
117975.note: Jewish Exponent: the Chabad in Cherry Hill 'was founded in 1993'; its own fundraising page: 'Founded in 1993'. (SJ Magazine has Rabbi Mendel and his wife arriving in 1994.) Its first synagogue was a donated Voorhees storefront; at 1925 Kresson Road, Cherry Hill, from 2002 (Chabad Lubavitch of Camden and Burlington Counties).

earlier.where: a donated storefront in Voorhees

117968.name: Valley Chabad
117968.note: IRS (GuideStar): Valley Chabad's ruling year 1997, so it existed by then. Jewish Standard (CrownHeights.info, 26 Oct 2006): 'After six years in a house on Overlook Road in Woodcliff Lake' (from about 2000), Rabbi Dov Drizin's group sought a 3.8-acre property. Start year not found yet.

earlier.where: a house on Overlook Road, Woodcliff Lake

118396.name: Chabad at Short Hills
118396.note: Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 31 Dec 2018, 'Milestone for Chabad of Short Hills: 22 Temporary Years, 1 Permanent Center'): 'It all started in 1995 when Rabbi Mendel and Chana Devora Solomon, then living in nearby Morristown and working for the Rabbinical College of America, were approached by a Short Hill's resident ... requesting assistance leading weekly Shabbat prayer services'; after decades in two small family homes, its permanent center opened in 2018. (An earlier Orthodox home minyan of Isadore Spiegel began in 1993.)

earlier.where: two small family homes in Short Hills (the Solomons commuted from Morristown for 16 years)

118465.name: Chabad Jewish Center of NWBC
118465.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of NW Bergen County was founded by Rabbi Chanoch and Mimi Kaplan in August 2000, as a Jewish Community Center'. North Jersey Record (CrownHeights.info, 17 May 2012): 'The center was established by Kaplan and his wife, Mimi, in 2000'; 'For 12 years we met at various locations', then the former Franklin Lakes Reformed Bible Fellowship church on Pulis Avenue (opened 6 May 2012).

earlier.where: various rented locations

118500.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Hoboken
118500.note: Lubavitch.com / Patch: Rabbi Moshe and Shaindel Schapiro founded the Chabad in 2001, having come to Hoboken to conduct Rosh Hashana services in September 2001; Chabad.org (24 Oct 2014): 'The rabbi and his wife started their programming in Hoboken in September 2001, just after 9/11'; Jewish Link (2025): 'When we first moved here 24 years ago'. Chabad.org (2014): it used temporary spaces for Shabbat services and meals until Hurricane Sandy (Oct 2012) washed them away, then the rabbi's own house; its first permanent home, the Weisfeld Family Chabad Jewish Center at 80 Park Ave., opened in Sept 2014 as Hoboken's first new synagogue in about 100 years. chabad.org now gives 720 Monroe Street. Entity: Chabad of Hoboken and Jersey City.

earlier.where: Hoboken: temporary spaces for Shabbat services and meals (washed away by Hurricane Sandy)
Hoboken: Rabbi Moshe Schapiro's house

118527.name: Chabad of South Brunswick
118527.note: South Brunswick Post (22 Aug 2002): Rabbi Levi and Goldie Azimov's Chabad Jewish Center, run from their home on Finnegans Lane, which he hoped to grow into a synagogue; CrownHeights.info (2013): its 10th anniversary dinner (postponed from Nov 2012); Jewish Link (2025): built 'over the past 23 years'. All point to 2002.

earlier.where: the Azimovs' home and office, Finnegans Lane

118485.name: Chabad of Lawrenceville
118485.note: IRS: 'Chabad Lubavitch Of Lawrenceville', ruling Oct 2003, so it existed by then. Rabbi Yitzhak Goldenberg also directs the Chabad/Young Israel of Lawrenceville (NJ Jewish News). Start year not found yet.

118518.name: Chabad of Union County
118518.note: IRS (GuideStar): Chabad of Union County, ruling year 2002, Rabbi Avrohom Blesofsky, so it existed by then. Start year not found yet.

3115859.name: Chabad Young Professionals - Morristown
3115859.note: COLlive, 30 March 2016: 'Just before Purim, Rabbi Moishe and Mushkie Gurevitz ... moved to Morristown, NJ as the new Shluchim to serve the Young Jewish Professional community in Morristown', appointed by Rabbi Moshe Herson with CYP of Merkos 302.

5038582.name: Chabad of Newark
5038582.note: COLlive, 16 Feb 2021: 'Rabbi Avraham and Mushka Minsky, were appointed as the new Chabad Shluchim in Newark'; 'Over the past few months, Rabbi and Mrs. Minsky (nee Paltiel) have been successfully active in the city' (so they began in late 2020).

6644585.name: Chabad of Ridgewood
6644585.note: COLlive, 22 Dec 2024: 'Rabbi Ashie and Sara Denebeim (nee Drizin) will be establishing a new Chabad Center in Ridgewood, NJ' (announced; the move followed).

6388831.name: Chabad of Summit
6388831.note: COLlive, 19 March 2024: 'The city of Summit, New Jersey now has its first Chabad Shliach'; Rabbi Mendy and Chana Marasow 'have opened up the first Chabad center, local to Summit'.

118547.name: Chabad of Randolph
118547.note: WRNJ (6 Jan 2026): 'Founded in 1987, Chabad of Randolph has served the township's growing Jewish community for decades'; its 3,000 sq ft complex on Hanover Avenue opened in 2023 (now the Hadar Family Foundation Center). Rabbi Avraham and Chava Bekhor today; reportedly begun by his mother, Devora Tilson, in her home.

118550.name: Chabad of Sussex County
118550.note: Sparta Independent (Nov 2017): 'Chabad of Sussex County, located at 266 Woodport Road in Sparta, was established in 2002'; Rabbi Mendel Dubov has led it since about 2011 (a Rabbi Lewis led it in 2006). In 2006 it moved into a Sparta plaza (CrownHeights.info).

118577.name: Chabad of Princeton University
118577.note: Several accounts: Rabbi Eitan Webb 'founded the Chabad House at Princeton in 2002'; he and Gitty Webb 'began Princeton's Chabad in 2002 in a narrow apartment near Nassau Street'; Jewish Link (2024): they arrived 'to launch the Scharf Family Chabad House 22 years ago'. In spring 2020 it bought the adjacent 17 Edwards Place.

earlier.where: a narrow apartment near Nassau Street

118587.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Monroe
118587.note: CrownHeights.info, 18 Oct 2015: 'As the Hakhel year began, just after Rosh Hashanah, hundreds filled the hall in celebration of the 13th anniversary' of the Chabad Jewish Center of Monroe Township (so fall 2002); a 2004 report: Rabbi Eliezer Zaklikovsky 'was sent to Monroe to start a new Chabad center about two years ago'. IRS: active from Feb 2003. (Its 10th-anniversary gala was held in Oct 2013.)

118603.name: Chabad of Hunterdon County
118603.note: CrownHeights.info, 8 June 2013: 'On Wednesday, May 29th Chabad of Hunterdon County celebrated its 10th Anniversary Dinner Banquet'; a 2009 banquet marked its sixth anniversary; elsewhere 'established in 2003 by Rabbi Eli and Rachel Kornfeld'. (One article and the IRS record say 2004.) Now in Annandale/Clinton Township.

118627.name: Chabad in Medford
118627.note: Burlington County Times (CrownHeights.info, 24 March 2014): Rabbi Yitzchok Kahan 'arrived in South Jersey 10 years ago, and used his small home as a meeting place and quasi-synagogue'; the Inquirer (June 2015): the group grew from fewer than 10 people meeting 12 years earlier at the Medford Community Center or Masonic Lodge (so 2003); another piece has him joining in 2007. New home on Main Street (74 S. Main St.) in 2014.

earlier.where: the Kahans' home; also the Medford Community Center and the local Masonic Lodge

150720.name: Chabad of Toms River
150720.note: Chabad.org: the Chabad House 'was founded in 2004'; Rabbi Moshe Gourarie (interview): cold calls starting in 2004; the Forward (2016): it had operated from the rabbi's home for 12 years when told it needed a variance. Began in a small house on New Hampshire Avenue; later the rabbi's home at 2001 Church Road (bought 2011). IRS entity: 2007.

earlier.where: a small house on New Hampshire Avenue
the rabbi's home, 2001 Church Road

416264.name: Chabad of Old Tappan
416264.note: The Jewish Standard (CrownHeights.info, about 30 June 2006, 'The Rebbe's New Soldier: Chabad to Open in Old Tappan'): Lubavitch on the Palisades will sponsor Rabbi Mendy Lewis to start a Chabad outpost in Old Tappan later that summer, serving Northvale, Rockleigh and Harrington Park; Anash (2024): a housewarming marking '18 years of Chabad Old Tappan'.

555228.name: Chabad of Gloucester County
555228.note: Chabad of Gloucester County 'was founded in 2007 by Rabbi Avi & Mina Richler'; Rabbi Richler (2017): 'When we came in 2007 to Gloucester County, we knew one Jewish family'. A permanent home (a former bed-and-breakfast in the historic district, 12 Woodstown Road) from 2011.

259220.name: Chabad of Northwest NJ - Western Region
259220.note: Recorder Community Newspapers (CrownHeights.info, 7 Nov 2007), on Rabbi Yaacov Shusterman's Chabad Jewish Center in Flanders (Mount Olive): 'The Chabad's Hebrew school ... started out as two students attending in 2004'; in 2007 the center was 'in its third year'; High Holiday services at the Flanders Crossing Recreation Center.

749411.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Holmdel
749411.note: New Jersey Jewish News (CrownHeights.info, 27 Oct 2008): Chabad of Western Monmouth County 'has established an outreach center for students attending Brookdale Community College. The new Chabad Jewish Center, which opened in early October, is located in the Holmdel residence of Rabbi Shmaya Galperin'; Asbury Park Press (CrownHeights.info, 10 March 2011): 'When I first came here three years ago ... I had only 20 people on the High Holy Days'. Later at 65 West Main Street.

earlier.where: Rabbi Shmaya Galperin's Holmdel residence

1418905.name: Anshei Lubavitch
1418905.note: Jewish Link (1 Nov 2017): 'Anshei Lubavitch, which was founded in 1909, has a number of sifrei Torah ... according to Rabbi Neubort, the shul's rabbi'. A business listing says it formed from a merger of three Paterson synagogues and moved to Fair Lawn in 1985. The year is the congregation's founding; when it came under a Chabad rabbi (Rabbi Levi Neubort) is not found.

earlier.where: Paterson, N.J. (before the move to Fair Lawn)

2021658.name: Chabad of Montclair
2021658.note: Baristanet (CrownHeights.info, 15 Sept 2014): Rabbi Yaacov and Ita Leaf 'are hoping to establish a Chabad presence in Montclair'; 'The Leafs moved to Montclair in July, from Crown Heights'; appointed by her father, Rabbi Boruch Klar of West Orange (ChabadInfo, 13 Sept 2014). Now 9 Carriage Way.

2298429.name: Chabad at Rowan University
2298429.note: Jewish Link (Sept 2024): the university 'has had a Chabad for 11 years since Rabbi Hersh Loschak and his wife, Fraidy, came to campus' (so 2013); Courier-Post (via AOL): the center 'celebrated its 10th year' in April 2023.

2676928.name: Chabad Community Center of Robbinsville and S. Hamilton
2676928.note: CrownHeights.info: 'Rabbi Chaiton and his wife Chana moved to Hamilton in 5774 – 2014, under the umbrella of Chabad of Mercer County' (her father, Rabbi Dovid Dubov); NJ Jewish News: the couple opened the Chabad house in Robbinsville in 2014, at first holding ceremonies at their home; the ninth center under Chabad of Mercer County.

earlier.where: the Chaitons' home

1539663.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life | Upper Passaic County
1539663.note: Jewish Standard (23 Sept 2011): Rabbi Mendy Gurkov's new Chabad Jewish Center of Upper Passaic County 'officially opened on Sept. 15 with a wine tasting and kabbalah lecture held at the Holiday Inn in Wanaque', holding events there or at the Gurkovs' home at first; later rented space in the Haskell Town Shopping Center, and a permanent home in 2024 (Jewish Link).

earlier.where: the Holiday Inn, Wanaque, and the Gurkovs' home
rented space in the Haskell Town Shopping Center

3186402.name: Chabad of West Orange
3186402.note: NJ Jewish News (2 July 2014): 'In 1996, before founding West Orange Chabad, Rabbi Boruch Klar and his wife, Devorah, opened a store' (Lubavitch Center Judaica, 456 Pleasant Valley Way); 'Three years later, they began running a beginners' service at Ahawas Achim B'nai Jacob & David' (1999); 'Within two years the service outgrew its space in that synagogue and moved to the store's basement'; Rabbi Mendy and Altie Kasowitz were hired to grow it. Its own building, 401 Pleasant Valley Way, was dedicated on June 14 (2015).

earlier.where: a beginners' service at Ahawas Achim B'nai Jacob & David
the basement of Lubavitch Center Judaica, 456 Pleasant Valley Way

2941342.name: Shabbat House
2941342.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 27 Nov 2017): 'The Klars began mapping out their plans for the Shabbat House in 2015, with the facility officially opening in August 2016.'

3423247.name: Chabad of South Bergen County and The Meadowlands
3423247.note: Jewish Standard (28 Sept 2014): Rabbi Yitzchok Lerman, 'who is affiliated with Chabad', is 'the new religious leader of Temple Beth-El in Rutherford'; he renamed it Congregation Beth-El Chabad, base of Chabad of South Bergen and the Meadowlands. The shul (founded 1919 as South Bergen Hebrew Institute, not Chabad) burned down on 8 Aug 2025.

earlier.where: Temple (Congregation) Beth-El, Rutherford (the same shul before it was Chabad; destroyed by fire 2025)

3235800.name: Chabad of Jackson
3235800.note: Lubavitch.com, 12 Sept 2016: 'Rabbi Shmulie and Musi Naparstek are moving to Jackson, New Jersey with their two daughters to open a new branch of Chabad'.

117656.name: Lubavitch Center of Essex County
117656.note: Jewish Link: their daughter Ita Leaf grew up in West Orange, 'where her parents have served as the directors of Chabad of Essex County since 1980' (Rabbi Boruch and Devorah Klar). The Lubavitch Center Judaica store at 456 Pleasant Valley Way opened in 1996; IRS ruling 2004.

3779812.name: Chabad of Closter
3779812.note: The center's own 'Meet Our Family' page: Rabbi Yossi Gluckowsky, invited by Rabbi Mordechai Shain (Lubavitch on the Palisades), founded the Closter shul in 2017. IRS ruling for its corporation 2019.

4173417.name: Chabad of Bayonne
4173417.note: Jewish Link: Rabbi Moshe and Chaya Schapiro (Hoboken) led intermittent activities in Bayonne 'until 2017, when Rabbi Yisrael and Shulamis Bennish came to establish a permanent Chabad house'.

earlier.where: Bayonne activities run from Chabad of Hoboken (Rabbi Moshe Schapiro)

4016283.name: Chabad of Hackensack
4016283.note: Jewish Link, 11 April 2018, 'First-Ever Chabad House to Open in Hackensack': just before Pesach Friends of Lubavitch of Bergen County agreed to acquire Temple Beth El's building at 280 Summit Avenue; 'the newly forming Chabad of Hackensack ... will be led by Rabbi Mendy Kaminker, who is moving to Hackensack in June from southern New Jersey'.
